p: valley of vision: Meaning, Judea, which was compassed about with mountains, and was called the valley of visions, because of the prophets, who were always there, whom they named Seers.
aileth thee now: He speaks to Jerusalem, whose inhabitants fled up to the housetops for fear of their enemies.
shoutings: Which was wont to be full of people and joy.
with the sword: But for hunger.
bound by the archers: And led into captivity.
far: Who have fled from other places to Jerusalem for comfort.
bitterly: He shows what is the duty of the godly, when God's plagues hang over the Church, and especially of the ministers, Jer 9:1.
crying to the mountains: That is, the shout of the enemies whom God had appointed to destroy the city.

bore the quiver with chariots of: He reminds them how God delivered them once from Sennacherib, who brought the Persians and Syrians with him, that they might by returning to God avoid that great plague which they would suffer by Nebuchadnezzar.
coverings of Judah: The secret place where the armour was: that is, in the house of the forest, 1Ki 7:2.
the breaches of the city of: You forfeited the ruinous places which were neglected in times of peace: meaning, the whole City, and the City of David, which was within the compass of the other.
of Jerusalem: Either to pull down such as might hurt, or else to know what men they were able to make.
water of the old pool: To provide if need should be of water.
its maker: To God who made Jerusalem: that is, they trusted more in these worldly means than in God.
eat and drink: Instead of repentance you were joyful and made great cheer, contemning the admonitions of the prophets saying Let us eat and drink for our prophets say that we will die tomorrow.

treasurer: Because the Hebrew word also signifies one who nourishes and cherishes, there are those of the scholars who think that this wicked man nourished a secret friendship with the Assyrians and Egyptians to betray the Church and to provide for himself against all dangers: in the mean season he packed craftily, and got of the best offices into his hand under Hezekiah, ever aspiring to the highest.
here: Meaning, that he was a stranger, and came up of nothing.
for himself in a rock: While he thought to make his name immortal by his famous sepulchre, he died most miserably among the Assyrians.
shame of thy lord's house: Signifying that whatever dignity the wicked attain to, at length it will turn to the shame of those princes by whom they are preferred.
call my servant Eliakim the son: To be steward again, out of which office he had been put, by the craft of Shebna.
key of the house of David: I will commit to him the full charge and government of the king's house.
nail in a sure place: I will establish him, and confirm him in his office, of this phrase read Ezr 9:9.
all vessels of small quantity: Meaning that both small and great who will come from Eliakim, will have praise and glory by his faithful officer.
nail that is fastened in the: He means Shebna, who in man's judgment should never have fallen.
